title: The Lambing Pen of Perhaps
tagline: Slide a corpse to the exact midpoint between two towns, build every possible world in an unwatched lambing pen to find what the kohen is guaranteed, split the plump lamb from the lean one, and load the gift tray for Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yosei
mechanic: precision-tape slider + premise-grid deduction + possible-worlds enumeration pen + jurisdiction-courtyard parable toggle + gift-tray loader. A range slider moves a slain body between two towns while a wobbling tape refuses to read an exact tie (the Rabbis: impossible to be precise); a 2×2 grid of premises (precision possible/impossible × kerova excludes/includes several towns) where the player derives no heifer / two heifers / one shared heifer with a stipulation, then seats the first tanna, Rabbi Eliezer and Rav Amram’s Rabbis in their cells (18a:2–6); seven unwatched lambing nights from the new mishna (two first-timers bearing 2M, M+F, 2M+F, 2F+M, 2M+2F; one experienced + one first-timer bearing 2M, M+F) where the player taps newborns into each ewe’s birth order to build worlds, tracks the lowest kohen yield found, declares the guaranteed count, and an exhaustive enumerator reveals the worst world (‘perhaps both bore females first’); a plump/lean hand-out under Rabbi Tarfon (better one to the kohen) and Rabbi Akiva per Rabbi Yoḥanan (kohen takes the lean; meshammenin = the shumman is disputed), the one-died contradiction resolved by Rabbi Ami’s retraction, Rabbi Ḥiyya’s shepherd and homeowner folds, and an SVG courtyard whose corner shades to the kohen when Rabbi Tarfon grants him a share (Rava/Rav Pappa, 18b:10–12); closed by toggling the foreleg/jaw/maw tray for Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yosei across the replacement-with-kohen case, Rabbi Elazar’s kohen-got-nothing case, and Rav Pappa’s uncertain-tithe case, each with its ‘lest you say’ pick

title: Whose Lamb Is It?
tagline: Count out Rabbi Tarfon's sela, shekel and ragya, pass lambs, donkeys and grain piles from hand to hand until someone is left holding them, then unlock why Rav Naḥman needed both of his inheritance rulings
mechanic: coin-purse composer + pass-the-parcel custody relay + two-dial tzerichuta lock. Tap sela/shekel/dinar/ma'a coins into a purse to pay exact amounts: Rabbi Tarfon's generous sela, miserly shekel and middle ragya (Rava: three dinars, ragil here and there), the one-ma'a lean lamb that works for one who acts on his own (vs. the ragya for one who comes to ask), and the donkey's full value when there's no lamb (Reish Lakish via Ravina's not-stricter-than-hekdesh, with Rav Naḥman son of Rav Yosef's boiled-vegetables option); then ten custody chains where a token steps hand to hand across an animated track before the player rules who ends up holding it: a stranger redeeming another's donkey (owner, by the thief's double-payment proof), ten doubtful donkeys' lambs (tithed and kept), the kohen's gift lamb (exempt from tithe), donkeys and tevel inherited through a kohen maternal grandfather (kept), gentile-smoothed vs. Jew-smoothed piles bought from a gentile (exempt by 'your grain' vs. tithed-and-his), produce deposited with a Samaritan vs. a gentile (Demai 3:4 and Rabbi Elazar's framing), and the lamb that died before reaching the kohen (his from separation); closed by a lock that opens only when both dials name the real tzerichuta reasons (lambs stand separated vs. grain tithed from itself)

title: The Donkey Nobody Redeemed
tagline: Sort carcasses between village and market and watch 'its prohibition is its intent' collapse, scrub a firstborn donkey from birth to the cleaver under Rabbi Yehuda and two readings of Rabbi Shimon, then balance the scale that decides whether a woman is betrothed with it
mechanic: village/market placement map + contradiction-finder + life-cycle timeline scrubber + legal-tool rack + balance-scale physics toy. Eight Okatzin 3:3 carcasses (non-kosher horse anywhere, kosher nevela anywhere, kosher bird and chelev in villages vs. markets, Rabbi Shimon's pig) drop onto a two-zone map and are ruled already-food vs. needs-intent, then the player multi-selects every ruling that refutes the issuro-chishuvo theory before the Gemara's reisha/seifa argument and Rava's conclusion, with a two-reading toggle on Nimos vs. Rabbi Eliezer's practice crow; a range-slider timeline of the firstborn donkey (alive: sale/rent value, alive: shearing/work, redeemed with a lamb, neck broken) where each stop is ruled permitted/forbidden under three lenses (Rabbi Yehuda; Rabbi Shimon per Rabba/Rav Nachman/Reish Lakish; Rabbi Shimon per Rabbi Yochanan), with the neck-break stop gated behind choosing the cleaver-from-behind over the reed/sickle/ax/saw/locked room; Rav Nachman's two proofs (the arifa gezera shava, Levi's lost-money baraita) each judged only-Rabbi-Shimon vs. Rabbi-Yehuda-could-be-the-tanna before Safra's and the Gemara's deflections; and an SVG balance scale for the Kiddushin 56b mishna where the player sets the donkey's value and toggles Rabbi Shimon / Rabbi Yehuda with an any-amount lamb / Rabbi Yehuda with Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda's shekel minimum until nothing is left in her hand (Rav's donkey-worth-a-shekel case), closed by picking Leviticus 27:25 as Rava's source for the shekel over Numbers 18:16's rejected hekesh

title: The Et Hunter
tagline: Shimon HaAmasoni expounded every little 'et' in the Torah until he reached 'Et the Lord your God you shall fear.' Hunt the particles yourself, stack the Gemara's proofs that milk is kosher and watch three of them crack, then climb a ladder of strange-calf dilemmas the Gemara leaves half-open
mechanic: particle-hunt word game + proof-tower judge + narrowest-reading ladder puzzle. Tap every אֶת (and the extra heh of ha-teme'im) across Exodus 20:12, Leviticus 11:4 and 11:31, earning coins for expounding (glosses: Ketubot 103a's stepparents and older brother, Rabbi Shimon's et ha-gamal = camel's milk, the heh = juice, gravy and sediment). Deuteronomy 6:13 unlocks last and forces the withdrawal choice, which sets the withdrawal counter equal to the expounding counter ('just as I received reward for expounding…') before Rabbi Akiva's Torah-scholars reveal. Then sort four camel derivations between Rabbi Shimon and the Rabbis. Next, judge six proofs that milk is kosher as hold or crack, naming the Gemara's objection for each one that cracks (benefit-vs-eating twice, sell-to-buy-food); the three that hold (David's ten cheeses with its 'commerce in wartime?' rebuttal, milk and honey, Isaiah 55:1) stack as bricks on a tower. Finally, pick exactly the rungs that two baraitot must cover in the cow→donkey / donkey→horse / cow→horse chain of dilemmas, where the Gemara narrows both to the first rung, then compare horns and hooves to reach the 'just a red donkey' answer, with an epilogue on Rabbi Shimon's head-and-most-of-the-body rule

title: Double or Nothing
tagline: A Roman officer named Kontrokos accuses Moses of cooking the books — a Levite headcount short 300 men, a treasury missing half its silver. Audit the census yourself, catch the Sanctuary's secret double-weight maneh, sort a litter of mismatched newborns, and unravel a rabbi's wordplay on Rephidim and Shittim
mechanic: forensic-audit ledger puzzle + drag-free verdict sorter + name/derash toggle cards — two real Kontrokos-vs-Rabban-Yoḥanan-ben-Zakkai ledger discrepancies (22,300 individually-counted Levites vs. the Torah's stated 22,000; 201 talents 11 maneh collected vs. 100 talents spent on sockets) worked as multiple-choice audits with full reveals of Abaye's dayo principle and the doubled Sanctuary maneh, plus a live one-sixth-from-the-outside padding slider deriving Ezekiel 45:12's 60-shekel maneh; a six-case litter sorter for the new mishna (cow→donkey-shaped calf, donkey→horse-shaped foal, ewe→goat-shaped lamb with and without partial simanim, ordinary goat kid, camel→kosher-looking newborn) where firstborn status and eating status are guessed as two independently-scored verdicts per case before the daf's real reasoning reveals; and a four-card dialogue between Rabbi Chanina and Rabbi Eliezer toggling between Rabbi Eliezer's literal place-names (Rephidim, Shittim) and Rabbi Yehoshua's derash readings from the parallel baraita

title: Called the People?
tagline: A Levite snatches gifts meant for the kohen and Rav can't decide whether to make him pay: is a Levite counted among "the people" who owe the foreleg, jaw, and maw? Work the gift docket on nine real cases, then follow four failed proofs — one a genuine refutation — before Mareimar closes the file for good, and catch the daf ending mid-sentence on Ulla and the kohenet
mechanic: three-bin repossession docket + multiple-choice doubt-proof gauntlet — nine real cases (untithed teruma, an undelivered foreleg/jaw/maw, gifts already in one kohen's hand, a poor owner keeping his own peret and olelot, withheld maaser ani, a cow's maw sold whole vs. by weight, unclaimed first-shorn wool, and an unsifted stew) sorted into מוֹצִיאִין / אֵין מוֹצִיאִין / פָּטוּר per the daf's actual sanctity, azivah-vs-netina, and intact-object tests, paired with a four-round gauntlet reconstructing Rav's real unresolved doubt over whether Levites are called 'the people' (the nine-kohen-properties baraita, the sanctity-principle baraita, the slaughter-for-whom baraita escalating into an explicit תיובתא, and Rav's own tannaitic-dispute rescue), closing on Mareimar's dual ruling and a click-to-reveal cliffhanger on Ulla, the kohenet, and the mincha law that the daf itself leaves mid-sentence

title: A Hair's Breadth
tagline: A dog that ate from a corpse lies dead across the threshold and four Tannaim rule on the house. Slide it, widen its neck, flip it around until the judges say what each challenge asks (or admit it cannot be done), fill Rabbi Shimon's two-of-three grid, scratch a thigh bone and a creeping thing's egg open by a hair's breadth, and go out and see the orifices, sinews, and seams that decide whether a touch reaches the flesh
mechanic: constraint-satisfaction sandbox with live judges + scratch-off canvas + lens-reveal hidden-object — an SVG doorway scene where the player sets three real variables of Oholot 11:7 as the Gemara reads it (mouth in/out, neck under a handbreadth / a handbreadth counting walls / a handbreadth of hollow, past the doorstop line or on the outer threshold) while four judge tiles rule live (Rabbi Meir on the neck, Rava's Rabbi Yosei on hollow-plus-position, Rabbi Elazar on the exit route, Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira always impure), and seven target-verdict challenges must be satisfied or declared impossible (Yosei-strict-and-Meir-lenient and ben-Beteira-pure are the traps); a 3×3 exactly-two-per-row-and-column logic grid for Rabbi Shimon's mould / barley-bone / golel-and-dofek across contact, carrying, and tent; a destination-out scratch canvas where a hair-thin stroke flips a sealed thigh bone or embryo egg from tahor to tamei, with Rav Oshaya's intent button and an embryo-tissue toggle; and nine cases (hide, kidney in fat, sealed and perforated bone, unbroken and tissueless eggs, half-earth mouse touched on either half, sea mouse) inspected with a draggable clip-path lens that reveals the orifices, sinews, and seams before ruling

title: Between Two Gates
tagline: A validly slaughtered animal is still twitching — out of the category of the living, not yet entered the category of the dead. Rule its ten real laws at the threshold (food impurity but not carcass impurity, the limb versus the flesh that parts from it, Abaye's double stringency, the trap of the invalid slaughter), probe the bird and the beast for the parts that are merely wood, and judge which gathering of alal carries carcass impurity
mechanic: liminal threshold tug-of-war + anatomy pin-probe — a heartbeat nefesh-orb hangs in a doorway between an ember Living Gate and a bone Dead Gate while the player rules the ten real mefarkeset laws of Rav Oshaya's Tosefta and Abaye (takes food impurity, no carcass impurity, separated limb like ever min hachai, separated flesh pure, forbidden to bnei Noach even after death, doesn't shield swallowed items under a corpse's roof, bestiality still liable, Rabbi Yoḥanan over Ḥizkiyya, plus one-siman and stabbing trap cards that collapse the doorway), each correct verdict tugging the orb toward a gate before it drifts back to dead center for Rabbi Zeira's 'left the living, never entered the dead'; opened by numbered pins over bird-and-beast line art ruling beak tip / Rav Pappa's inner membrane, talon tip / base sunk in flesh, and horn shaft / blood-line base as 'joins' or 'merely wood', and closed by picking which of three alal collectors (adult, child, wind) creates carcass impurity per Rav Huna's da'at rule and whether the hide nullifies two clinging half-olives

title: The Soul That Drinks
tagline: Work the alchemist's bench: congeal the blood, melt the forbidden fat, dissolve the chametz, liquefy a bird carcass over fire and over sun — stamp each verdict, then find the stringency that blocks each of the Gemara's attempted derivations, forge the one source-pair that carries consecrated produce, and swing the two exegetical lenses of Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua
mechanic: state-change alchemy bench + refutation forge — eight substances visibly change state in an animated flask (melt over fire, dissolve in water, congeal, rot in the sun) before the player stamps the daf's real verdict (Reish Lakish's three nefesh-includes-the-drinker readings, the sun-rotted carcass that stays pure, the lentil-bulk of sheretz gravy, liquids-don't-join-solids), then a derivation-blocking logic game where the player identifies the shared stringency that refutes each proposed source (karet, no period of fitness, never permitted, any-amount impurity, dayo) and forges the one valid source-pair for hekdesh liquids from bikkurim/teruma/chametz/carcass, capped by an Eliezer/Yehoshua don-minah lens toggle flipping the verdicts on date honey, apple wine, bikkurim beverages, and orla juice

title: The Master Said to Me
tagline: Host one Babylonian evening meal and survive it: patrol the fields at dusk, wash three kinds of waters correctly, wait out the cheese after meat, wipe with the one bread Rabbi Zeira allows, guard your crumbs from the angel of poverty, sink the foam, untie the gardener's bundle, and keep the wine barrel out from under the gutter demon
mechanic: hazard-navigation dinner simulator — an eleven-scene choose-your-action evening meal scored on three meters (guf/body, mamon/purse, ruach/spirit) where every choice is resolved by the daf's actual rulings (Rav Chisda's meat-then-cheese ban, Rabbi Zeira's wiping-bread tests, the first/middle/final waters baraita, Sodomite salt, the held-cup limits), with a signature flip-card after each of Abaye's eight traditions that turns his assumed mundane reason over to reveal Rabba's hidden one (evil spirit, poverty angel, witchcraft, demons), graded on Mar Ukva's vinegar-son-of-wine scale

title: The Angel Who Never Sang
tagline: Stage the angel's grip to see which thigh Yaakov lost, match five Sages to the five verses that keep a scholar indoors after dark, measure the ladder at eight thousand parasangs, and re-cut the angels' Kedushah until the Divine Name lands where the baraita allows it
mechanic: top-down staging puzzle placing the angel in the three real positions the Sages reconstruct (face-to-face hug per Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi and Rashi, at Yaakov's right hand per Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani's gentile and Rava bar Ulla's Torah scholar, or up from behind per the Rabbis) and reading off which thigh each blocking strikes, a five-verse/five-Sage single-use assignment of the sources for a Torah scholar not going out alone at night (Rabbi Yitzchak, Rabbi Abba bar Kahana, Rabbi Abbahu, the Rabbis, Rav), an evidence-dial derivation of the ladder's 8,000-parasang width from the plural of olim/yordim and Tarshish's 2,000, and a Kedushah composer where the player adds and removes kadoshes across three angelic companies until Rav Chananel's 1/1/1 becomes the Gemara's emended 1/2/3, validated live against the baraita's rule that angels may not utter the Name before three words, plus a seven-stop dial through the disputed frequency of the angels' song

title: Larger Than Life
tagline: Catch the Mishnah itself exaggerating across the ash-mound, golden vine, and Curtain, route seven real sciatic-nerve cases through the altar's back rooms, and follow the Gemara's own back-and-forth over whether Rabbi Yehuda was certain or just guessing
mechanic: spot-the-exaggeration reveal across three real Mishnayot (ash-mound, golden vine, Curtain) per Rabbi Yitzchak bar Nachmani/Shmuel's three guzma cases, a routing puzzle sending the sciatic nerve of burnt/peace offerings to their correct real destination (altar ash-mound vs. courtyard drain) per Rav Huna and the Rabbis, and a locked step-by-step reveal of the Gemara's certain-vs-unsure back-and-forth over Rabbi Yehuda's thigh ruling

title: What Are We?
tagline: Match three tzaddikim who called themselves dust, nothing, and a worm against five kings who crowned themselves gods, watch Rava rank humility itself, quiz the brand-new mishnah of gid hanasheh, and solve the ash-of-a-doomed-city riddle that closes the chapter
mechanic: 16-card memory-match grid pairing three self-effacing tzaddikim (Avraham, Moshe & Aharon, David) and five self-aggrandizing kings (Nimrod, Pharaoh, Sancheriv, Nevuchadnetzar, Chiram) to their real verses, followed by an interactive reveal of Rava's ranking that Moshe & Aharon's "what are we" outranks Avraham's "dust and ashes" plus flip-cards on Rabbi Il'a, Rabbi Abbahu, and Rabbi Yitzchak's humility teachings, a true/false quickfire on the six real conditions and two disputes of the brand-new gid hanasheh mishnah, and a step-by-step reveal of the idolatrous-city-ash logic (Ze'eiri's dust-of-its-dust distinction, Rava's mitzvot-lo-lehanot-nitnu, and Rav Ashi's shiur-based resolution) that closes the Kisuy HaDam chapter

title: Dust and Ashes
tagline: Sort sixteen real substances into what covers slaughtered blood and what doesn't, get stranded without earth once in the desert and once on a ship, and meet Beit Hillel and Beit Shammai's fight over whether ash even counts as dust
mechanic: substance sorting game (16 real mishna/baraita items dragged into 'covers'/'does not cover' bins, checked against the min-afar category and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel's grows-plants rule) + a desert/ship stranded-without-earth scenario picker (grind a gold dinar or burn your garment for ash) + a sage-position quiz on the dam hanitaz machloket + closing flip-cards on the Beit Hillel/Beit Shammai ash-is-afar dispute and Rava's aggada about Avraham's dust and ashes

title: One Covering for All
tagline: A deaf-mute, an imbecile, or a minor slaughters unsupervised — fill in Rebbi's real verdict grid, test whether a purity shortcut transfers to forbidden meat, then run animals through one covering pit and watch Rabbi Yehuda split it in two
mechanic: predict-and-reveal verdict grid (2×3 table exposing that the Rabbis actually dispute both clauses of the mishna, not just the one the plain text shows) + true/false twist cards flipping who's really lenient vs. stringent + a mi'ut/chazakah rule-transplant test + a group-and-seal sequencing toy (drop chaya/of tokens into a shared covering under the Rabbis' rule, or under Rabbi Yehuda's order-constrained split)

title: The Redacted Rabbis
tagline: Unmask which sage is hiding behind "the Rabbis" in two mirror-image mishnayot, catch each one's one real exception, and help Rabbi Chiyya outwit the moths in his flax
mechanic: redacted-ruling unmasking (reveal evidence chips, then accuse Rabbi Meir or Rabbi Shimon of hiding behind the mishnah's anonymous "the Rabbis" across two mirror-image rulings on unfit slaughter) + true/false loophole cards testing each sage's one real concession + a branching how-do-you-get-the-blood puzzle from Rabbi Chiyya's moth-eaten flax

title: The Stewpot Ledger
tagline: Slide your fortune from a hundred dinars to ten thousand and watch Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya's stewpot fill — then guess the bracket for six purses, diagnose a cup of lukewarm water, and flip five household maxims from Proverbs
mechanic: wealth-bracket resource simulator + predict-the-tier quiz (drag a log-scale dinar slider through Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya's four stewpot brackets, then guess the right pot and frequency for six purses) plus a branching diagnose-your-cup wizard for Rabbi Yochanan's lukewarm-water rule and a flip-card gallery of five Proverbs-derived household maxims

title: The Litter Ledger
tagline: A firstling drops its afterbirth, a consecrated ewe drops hers — split a hundred births into buckets and watch the majority decide their fate
mechanic: population majority scale (drag a genuine miut anywhere in range and watch Rav Ika's rov/miut bucket-arithmetic hold; toggle firstling vs. consecrated litters to flip which bucket wins)

title: The Convergence Gauge
tagline: Feel out which cords count as the convergence of sinews, then flip switches on three strands and watch Ameimar and Mar bar Rav Ashi disagree in real time
mechanic: diagnostic classifier + live dual-rule strand calculator (sort specimens by Abaye's four tests, then toggle three strands and watch two amoraic AND/OR formulas diverge)

title: The Warning Cry
tagline: Eight slaughters, one day — cry the hatra'ah only at the moment, and about the charge, that makes the lashes stick
mechanic: forewarning timeline (cry or hold your peace at each moment of a day's slaughters; hatra'at safek strikes doubtful cries)

title: The Koy Pen
tagline: Two hybrid kids, two different mothers — sort six real rulings into the right pen, then meet five sages who can't agree what a koy even is
mechanic: sort/spot-the-difference (assign six of Rav Pappa's real rulings to the correct sire×dam pen) + sage-to-claim matching + step-through objection volley

title: The Rispak Stables
tagline: Rabbi Abba wants mules for his wagon — listen to each bray, measure ears and tails, and harness only the ones that match
mechanic: siman inspection (hear synthesized brays, read ears & tails, yoke matching mules; koy-gate epilogue)

title: The Sealed Dockets
tagline: Seven verdict records survived the archive; set the four dials and reconstruct the cases of Oto v'et Beno
mechanic: inverse deduction (read the verdict stamps, set dials to reconstruct the case)

title: The Herdbook Lens
tagline: One womb-born kid becomes a three-generation herd — swing the lens of four poskim over the flock, stamp every page, and outrun the bear
mechanic: posek lens (swing rulings-lenses over one womb-born herd and stamp who needs the knife)

title: The Five-Year Lamb
tagline: Shepherd the ben pekuah from the womb to five years plowing the field — at every waypoint, is it one animal or part of another?
mechanic: waypoint trail (escort one creature through nine stations of its halakhic biography)

title: The Phantom Knife
tagline: Six scenes, one blade that never touches anything: click where the halakhic cut falls
mechanic: phantom-knife scene cuts (place the halakhic cut on an SVG scene, or keep it sheathed)

title: The Severed Link
tagline: Forge four chains of the daf's reasoning, link by link, in the smithy of Pumbedita
mechanic: chain-forging (pick the next link to rebuild the sugya's reasoning)

title: The Swallowed Ring
tagline: You are the posek: rule tamei or tahor on ten real cases of encapsulated impurity
mechanic: verdict cards (judgment quiz)
